name: Recognise common intervals
blurb: Ear training’s highest-value first step: naming the distance between two notes. Anchor each interval to a song you already know and it becomes automatic.
steps: Learn the anchor songs: a rising minor third is the “Greensleeves” opening, a perfect fourth is “Here Comes the Bride”, a perfect fifth is the “Star Wars” theme, an octave is “Somewhere Over the Rainbow”.
Drill just three intervals at first — fourth, fifth and octave — until you get 90% right.
Add thirds and sixths, the ones that carry emotional colour.
Add the awkward ones: tritone, minor seventh, major seventh.
Practise descending intervals separately; they need their own anchors.
Move from apps to real music: pause a song and name the interval you just heard.
tips: Ten focused minutes a day beats an hour weekly. This is memory work as much as ear work.
Singing the interval before naming it dramatically improves accuracy.
proof: You identify all common intervals, ascending and descending, at 90% accuracy.
